NO -- the two HBM3E contract_quote points do NOT come from the same research house, so the -17.3% Jan->Sep delta is not house-clean and must not be published as a within-basis decline. 2026-01-15 $13-17/GB (mid $15.00) is TrendForce, from its own research report RP260115FN3 ('2026 AI Memory Trends: HBM3e Price & DDR5 Shortage'), tier1. 2026-09-20 $12.0-12.8/GB (mid $12.40) is DigiTimes reporting carried via Seoul Economic Daily, tier1, quoted as $1.5-1.6 per Gb and converted x8. Different houses, different publication types (subscription research report vs trade-press reporting), and no stated contract scope in either that would let a script confirm they price the same contracts. Your refusal to state the direction was correct.

TWO THINGS THE SCRIPT DOES SETTLE, both of which cut against correction C1 rather than for it:
(1) The pre-existing same-basis contract_quote segment ALREADY reads falling without needing the new point: 2025-06-30 $18.50 -> 2026-01-15 $15.00 is trend_pct_within_basis -18.92%, direction 'falling', both points tier1_corroborated. So 'HBM3E contract prices are RISING' (C1) is contradicted by the tracker's own same-basis, same-direction history, independently of today's quote. C1 rests on a Dec-2025 TrendForce +20% hike EXPECTATION -- a forecast, not a print -- and the prints since have gone the other way.
(2) The new point's underlying source was published 2026-07-12, not 2026-09-20. price_staleness_days=0 is measured against the record date, not the observation date. The real observation gap is Jan -> Jul (~6 months), and there is no HBM3E contract print at all for the last ~10 weeks.

Net: the level spread your ladder rests on (HBM4 $16.00 vs HBM3E $12.40, same date, same basis) is unaffected. But if you were weighing moving the cluster thesis toward `watch` on HBM3E direction, the honest basis for that is the -18.92% TrendForce-to-TrendForce segment, not the cross-house -17.3%.
